title: Winning the Piece Back
subtitle: The same idea in a harder position

source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter I, §4 Some Winning Positions in the Middle-game, Example 12

steps.title: A piece behind
steps.source: White is a piece behind, and unless he can win it back quickly he will lose.

narration.say: White is a piece behind. Unless he wins it back quickly, he will lose.
Notice the same pattern as before: queen on h3, bishop on b2, black pawn on g6.

steps.title: Your turn: start with a capture

narration.say: Your move. Start by taking something.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Take a black piece.

feedback.*: The knight on d4 can take a black knight.

exercise.success: 1. Nxc6. Black does not take back: he plays Bg5, attacking the rook.

steps.title: Why Black cannot take
steps.source: He cannot take the Kt because White threatens mate by Q x P ch followed by R - R 3 ch.

narration.say: Why did Black not take the knight? Because of the idea from the last lesson.
Queen takes h7, check, then rook to h3, check, and mate.
Now Black's bishop attacks the rook on e3. White has a strong reply.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Use the knight with check.
exercise.success: 2. Ne7, check. Black takes with the queen.

steps.title: Your turn: the double attack
steps.source: 3 R x Q, B x R; 4 Q - Q 7 and White wins one of the two Bishops.

narration.say: Rook takes the queen, bishop takes the rook.
Now one queen move attacks both black bishops.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Attack both bishops at once.

feedback.*: Find a square from which the queen attacks b7 and e7.

exercise.hint: The queen goes to the seventh rank.
exercise.success: 4. Qd7. White wins a bishop, and with queen and bishop against rook and bishop he should win easily.

steps.title: What we learned
steps.source: These two examples show the danger of advancing the K Kt P one square, after having Castled on that side.

narration.say: These two examples show a danger: after castling, advancing the knight's pawn one square weakens the king.
A threat of mate can be used to win material.
